svg.aria-label: How to write ा: 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ा
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ा (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 47 (ा, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 55 of the 81 stored prototypes of the aa sign (68%) are one pen-down stroke, and 54 of those 55 move downward (49 start at the top): the stem, drawn from the top. 23 of the 81 (28%) are two strokes: the stem first, then a short top stroke, drawn left to right in 20 of the 23. The signs were collected without the headline, which is why most writers drew the stem alone; the bundled font prints the sign with a piece of headline on top, so the path draws that piece as the two-stroke writers do, after the stem, as the cited आ draws its headline after its trailing stem. Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant or the headline; that place is cited separately (compositionSource), and it is the one Devanagari sign a composed word may hold. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
